title: Population-based eigenstates of the SU(d) spin-exchange model for high-spin fermions in optical lattices
abstract: We investigate the $\mathrm{SU}(d)$ spin exchange model describing ultra-cold fermionic atoms with spin $s\ge 1$ in a one-dimensional optical lattice. The model emerges from the Fermi-Hubbard model in the strongly interacting regime with one atom in each lattice site. The central result of this work is the systematic construction of SE eigenstates in terms of magnetic sub-level populations. This representation provides a natural description of high-spin fermionic systems, where the underlying $\mathrm{SU}(d)$ symmetry gives rise to extensive degeneracies. We illustrate the usefulness of this framework for deriving effective Hamiltonians for a system weakly coupled to light through spin-orbit interactions, using a second-order Schrieffer--Wolff transformation projected onto the introduced population eigenbasis. These effective models provide a controlled description of the collective spin dynamics and capture the role of population redistribution among different collective spin length sectors induced by interactions. The agreement with the exact Fermi--Hubbard with light coupling dynamics confirms the consistency of the population eigenstates framework as a basis for describing high-spin quantum many-body systems.
summary: The paper develops a sophisticated theoretical framework using Population Eigenstates (PESs) to describe high-spin fermionic atoms in optical lattices governed by an SU(d) spin-exchange model. By projecting the dynamics onto this PES basis, the authors derive effective Hamiltonians that accurately capture complex collective spin behavior and quantum correlations when coupling to external fields like light.
main_problem: The central goal is systematically constructing eigenstates for the SU(d) spin-exchange model governing high-spin fermions in optical lattices.
main_result: The Population Eigenstate (PES) framework provides a natural basis that allows for describing collective spin dynamics and accurately modeling coupling to light, even when the total collective spin length is not conserved.
method: The authors employ systematic construction of eigenstates using PESs, deriving effective Hamiltonians via second-order Schrieffer–Wolff transformations projected onto these population manifolds.
model_or_system: The system involves ultra-cold fermionic atoms with high spin ($s \ge 1$) in a 1D optical lattice, modeled by the SU(d) spin exchange (SE) Hamiltonian derived from the Fermi-Hubbard model in the strongly interacting limit.
key_observables: Spin squeezing parameter ($\xi^2$), collective spin length ($\langle\hat{J}^2angle$), and population distribution among different spin sectors ($\langle\hat{P}_{E=0}(\Lambda)angle$).
important_parameters: High spin $s \ge 1$, strong interaction limit ($U \gg J$), quasi-momentum $q$, and coupling phase $\phi$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the strongly interacting regime for deriving the SE Hamiltonian, and effective Hamiltonians are derived using second-order perturbation theory.
figures_summary: Figures compare spin dynamics ($\xi^2$, $\langle\hat{J}^2angle$) between the full model, the PES-derived effective Hamiltonian, and a restricted Dicke manifold approximation for various coupling phases.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the SE model and introducing the PES basis (commuting with population operators) to deriving effective Hamiltonians via Schrieffer–Wolff transformations. It then analyzes the structure of spin eigenstates ($\Lambda$) within this basis, culminating in applying these tools to study dynamics under light coupling.
why_interesting: This work extends quantum many-body physics beyond the standard spin-1/2 limit by utilizing SU(d) symmetry, providing a powerful theoretical tool for understanding complex collective spin behavior in ultracold atomic systems.
